cells.tense: You are keeping a fair exchange going, and you can feel the give and take running cleanly between you and the work.
cells.ask: Name one thing you regularly put into your practice, and one thing it regularly hands back, so you can see both side by side.
cells.core:
There's a small light you keep lit, and repetition is what keeps it lit. Not a big push, just showing up and doing the thing again. The practicing is steady, and the fairness inside it stays even. You're not counting every coin. You put in what the practice asks, it gives back what you need to keep going, and you can pick it up the next day without bracing.

What holds this steady is that you keep letting it move. The work is something you can set down and trust to be there when you come back. That trust is the quiet part of this balance, and the price of it is the ordinary return. Not perfectly. Regularly. That returning is the exchange, and it's already yours.
cells.sheetLine: Your practice is a fair exchange you can keep making.
cells.verb: to keep a fair exchange moving between yourself and what you practice
cells.place: at a small, steadily kept practice

cells.tense: You will keep pushing the exchange past what the day can carry, waiting for it to prove itself equal.
cells.ask: Before adding one more thing to the practice, sit with what's already there for a full minute and notice what it has already given back.
cells.core:
The fairness of this exchange is under a microscope. Each round of practice gets checked — was that enough, is it coming back at the rate you expected, should there be more to show for it. The checking is loud, and it's stealing the stillness the practice was supposed to give you. You're ahead of the thing, bracing for a verdict that hasn't happened.

What you're reaching for isn't more effort. It's the ability to hold what you've made without squeezing it. Hold without forcing. Let one day's practice be exactly what it is, and see what comes back when no one is standing over it with a ledger. What needs doing today will still need doing.
cells.sheetLine: You're auditing the practice instead of letting it work.
cells.verb: to keep a fair exchange moving between yourself and what you practice
cells.place: at a small, steadily kept practice

cells.tense: You put the practice down at some earlier point, and the giving side of it has stayed quiet since.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing you used to do well, do it once for ten minutes, and pay attention to the single part that actually feels right.
cells.core:
The practice sits on the other side of a door you already walked through, unlit. You can feel the shape of what it used to be. Lately more of the exchange is on the receiving end — things come in, little goes out in the form of steady work — and that lop-sidedness has made the whole thing feel like something that happens to you rather than something you do.

What's starved is the ability to tell what's worth keeping in a practice from what's just noise. That kind of careful attention is its own small exercise, and it doesn't take much. Do it once with something you already do well, and let what you notice do the feeding.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped giving to the practice. Start with one careful look.

cells.tense: The sentence has been running unstated: you weigh what is fair between you and the work, and you let the work take the blame for the verdict.
cells.ask: Say one sentence out loud that begins with 'I decided' about how much you give to your practice, and stop there.
cells.core:
There's a courtroom running in the background of your practice. Terms get set, evidence gets weighed, and the verdict is whether today counts as enough. The practice appears to be the one making the demands, keeping its own score. It isn't. The deciding is being done, sentence by sentence, before any practice starts.

A calmer way of knowing what's fair is already at work in you, and it doesn't need the arguments. It arrives before you speak, lands without much fuss, and usually turns out to be right. You don't have to declare anything big. Notice that the answer showed up before the words did, and hold it for a second before handing it off to the work to explain.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one keeping the score even. Say so.
